answers.text: Situation: our help-center content platform served more than a million people a day in over 50 locales, and launches were stalling between product, ops, and backend. Task: I needed a design that could grow, survive a region failure, and stay fast. Action: I led the design with a document store, a GraphQL API, and cross-region caching, and I worked with ops on the rollout plan. Result: the service held about 200 millisecond latency and stayed available across regions.

answers.text: Situation: I owned creator monetization and notification services used by hundreds of clients and more than a thousand campaigns. Task: the services had to stay stable as query volume grew. Action: I changed the storage keys to use partitioning and composite keys so hot ranges split cleanly. Result: throughput rose by about 40 percent, from 16 thousand to 22.5 thousand queries a day.

answers.text: Situation: the same priority-zero incidents kept coming back and pulling the team off planned work. Task: I needed fewer incidents and clearer standards for newer engineers. Action: I traced the failures across team boundaries, set an error-handling standard, and coached two junior engineers on a three-month plan. Result: those repeat incidents stopped, and their reviews started catching the same class of bug before merge.
